sections.h2: How is property tax set up for a house seller in Alamance County?
sections.html:
One department, Alamance County Tax Administration, lists and values all taxable property and also collects the money. The department is at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and its phone line is (336) 228-1312.

The county was formed in 1849 from part of Orange County and covers about 434 square miles. Graham is the seat and Burlington is the largest community. The towns of Elon, Haw River, Green Level, Ossipee, Swepsonville and Alamance, plus parts of Mebane and Gibsonville, fall inside the county. Textile mills along the Haw River drove its early growth.

For a seller, the practical points are the January 1 listing date, the September 1 due date, the 2027 revaluation, and the delinquent tax check that happens when a deed is recorded. The sections below take each in turn.

sections.h2: What is the Alamance County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The county's land records page explains that property is listed in the name of the owner as of January 1, and that date sets the tax year. Bills are mailed in July and are due September 1, with no interest through January 5.

Alamance County tax and relief dates drawn from the county tax pages
DateWhat happens
January 1Listing date; owner on this day is billed
January 1 to 31Filing window for present-use and exemption applications
June 1Deadline for elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran relief
JulyBills mailed
September 1Bills due
January 5Last day to pay with no interest
January 6Delinquent; 2% interest added, then 0.75% on the sixth of each later month

A purchase that closes after January 1 can still produce a bill in the previous owner's name, even though the deed is recorded and the county has updated its record. Getting the mailing address corrected before July is the surest way to receive the bill on time.

Payment options are by mail (counted by postmark), in an indoor or outdoor drop box (credited as of the drop date), or online with a convenience fee. Registered vehicles are billed separately by the state through Tag and Tax Together at registration renewal.

sections.h2: What is happening with the 2027 revaluation in Alamance County?
sections.html:
Alamance County is revaluing every parcel effective January 1, 2027, and notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. North Carolina requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, and the county has chosen a four-year cycle.

Vincent Valuations, which assisted with the 2023 work, is performing the 2027 appraisal. Staff spend roughly two years in the field checking property features, comparing sales, and noting improvements. The county says its goal is to reach, or come close to, 100% of market value at revaluation.

A higher value does not automatically mean a higher bill. The county explains that tax rates come down when values go up, and that a revenue neutral rate would leave the average owner paying about the same as before. Owners whose values climbed faster than the county average tend to pay more, and those whose values lagged tend to pay less.

If you plan to sell in 2027, read the notice when it arrives. The appeal window is tied to the date on the notice, and the county warns that late appeals generally cannot be accepted. The revaluation hotline is the same number as the tax department, (336) 228-1312.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a property value in Alamance County?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review by the Tax Administration appraisers, then go to the Board of Equalization and Review if that fails. The county says real property appeals may be filed informally or formally, and the appeal window depends on the kind of property.

  • Real property: during the annual listing period, with documentation such as sales, photos, repair estimates or an appraisal.
  • Business and individual personal property: within 30 days of the date on the notice of value.
  • Registered motor vehicles: within 30 days of the due date on the tag and tax notice.

The state describes the next steps. The local board begins its work around the first week of April, gives you a set time to present your case, and sends a written decision. If you still disagree, you may appeal to the Property Tax Commission, which meets monthly in Raleigh, follows the rules of evidence, and places the burden of proof on the taxpayer.

Common grounds listed by the county are a value above what the property would sell for, wrong square footage or condition on the record, and neighborhood sales that support a lower number. The county also offers a comparable sales tool and a property record search for gathering evidence.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs can Alamance County homeowners use?
sections.html:
Most relief applications are due June 1, and several carry income limits that the state changes from year to year. Ask the tax department for the current figures before applying. The county also runs an online eligibility calculator for the elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the home's taxable value for owners who are 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and who meet the income limit.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: lets qualifying owners defer part of the tax on a permanent residence, based on a percentage of income. The owner must be 65 or older, or disabled, and must have owned and lived in the home at least five years.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes the first $45,000 of assessed value for honorably discharged veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability, or a surviving spouse. There is no age or income limit.
  • Present-use value: taxes qualifying farm, horticulture and forestry land on its use, but taxes deferred for the previous three years can be recaptured if the land leaves the program.

An owner who sells while a deferral or present-use status is in place should ask about payoff or recapture amounts before agreeing to a closing date.

sections.h2: What does Alamance County check about taxes when a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds states that every deed recorded after May 2, 2011, except timber deeds and releases, must go before the county Tax Department for delinquent tax certification first. That step follows G.S. 161-31(b). A seller with back taxes should plan to clear them so the certification can be issued.

After recording, the change reaches the property record through a short chain. The Register of Deeds keeps the document and gives it a book and page number. Land Records staff read it, update the owner name and mailing address, and publish the change to the online record and GIS map. A simple sale of an existing parcel moves faster than a split or a new subdivision. If you do not see the change after several weeks, call Land Records with the book and page number.

When an owner has died, ownership is established through an estate filed with the Clerk of Superior Court or through recorded documents. Taxes stay due on schedule while the title is sorted out, and the county asks for the estate file number, the parcel number or address, and a mailing address for future bills.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Alamance County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 171,415 residents in 2020 and estimates 186,177 for July 2025, a gain of 8.6% from the 2020 base. The 2020 to 2024 figures show a median owner-occupied value of $241,500, 65.0% owner occupancy and 70,062 households. Median gross rent was $1,064 and median household income was $65,651.

Builders took out 2,027 permits in 2025. Poverty stood at 13.8%, and workers averaged 25.9 minutes of travel to work.

Check your parcel on the county property record search before you set an asking price.

faqs.q: When are Alamance County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1. Interest does not start until January 6, so a bill paid by January 5 carries none. After that, 2% is added, plus 0.75% on the sixth of each following month.

faqs.q: Who is billed if I buy a house after January 1?
faqs.a: The county lists property in the name of the owner as of January 1, so the bill may still arrive in the previous owner's name. Settle the split at closing and update the mailing address before July.

faqs.q: When will new values from the 2027 revaluation arrive?
faqs.a: Notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027, for the January 1, 2027 effective date. Your appeal deadline is tied to the date on that notice.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief programs in Alamance County?
faqs.a: June 1 for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferral and the disabled veteran exclusion. Present-use and exemption filings fall in the January listing window.

faqs.q: Who do I call at Alamance County Tax Administration?
faqs.a: Call (336) 228-1312 or visit 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The same number handles revaluation questions.
